changes.subject: New-Guid
changes.title: `New-Guid` emits a time-sortable UUID v7 by default instead of a random UUID v4
changes.detail: The output type and format are unchanged, which is what makes this dangerous: a script keeps working, but its identifiers become predictable. Time-ordered UUIDs leak creation time and are guessable in sequence, so anything using `New-Guid` as a secret or a nonce becomes weaker without any visible change.
changes.migration: A script that needs a fully random GUID must call `[guid]::NewGuid()` directly rather than `New-Guid`. Never use either as a security token: use a CSPRNG.

changes.subject: Format-Table, Format-List, Format-Custom
changes.title: `ValidateNotNullOrEmpty` added to `-Property`
changes.detail: Confirmed against the reference implementation: `Format-Table` `-Property` carries no validation attributes in 7.6.5, so passing an empty string succeeds there and throws in 7.7.
changes.migration: Filter empty values out of a `-Property` list before passing it.

changes.subject: argument validation
changes.title: Not-null-not-empty validation now throws ArgumentException instead of PSArgumentNullException
changes.detail: The exception type changes from `System.Management.Automation.PSArgumentNullException` to `System.ArgumentException`, so a catch block filtering on the old type stops matching.
changes.migration: Catch `System.ArgumentException`, or catch both types during a migration window.

changes.subject: Where-Object
changes.title: Explicit -<Operator>:$false is now honoured rather than treated as present
changes.detail: A switch parameter written as `-Not:$false` was previously indistinguishable from -Not. This is the general shape of a whole family of 7.7 fixes and is why the binder must model switch semantics rather than mere presence.

changes.subject: New-TemporaryDirectory
changes.title: `New-TemporaryDirectory` cmdlet added
changes.detail: Makes a temp directory a first-class concept, which means the virtual filesystem needs a real `/tmp` provider rather than an ordinary directory that happens to be named tmp.

changes.subject: Format-Table, Format-List, Format-Custom
changes.title: `-ExcludeProperty` parameter added to Format-* cmdlets
changes.detail: Confirmed absent in 7.6.5 by the captured command metadata. Belongs to the formatter, which is why formatting has to be separable from the command.

changes.subject: Join-Path
changes.title: `-Extension` parameter added
changes.detail: Confirmed absent in 7.6.5 by the captured command metadata.

changes.subject: $PSApplicationOutputEncoding
changes.title: Automatic variable controlling how native command output is decoded
changes.detail: Requires an encoding broker between the object pipeline and the native byte pipeline: without one, native output is decoded once, wrongly, and cannot be recovered.

changes.subject: Export-Csv
changes.title: `-Append` and `-NoHeader` are now mutually exclusive
changes.migration: Pick one. A script passing both now fails parameter binding.

changes.subject: Csv cmdlets
changes.title: `-NoTypeInformation` is an obsolete no-op; `-IncludeTypeInformation` is evaluated by value

changes.subject: ConvertFrom-Csv, ConvertTo-Csv, `Export-Csv`, Import-Csv, Get-Random, Get-SecureRandom, Get-TimeZone, Get-Uptime, `New-Guid`, New-PSSession, Split-Path, Test-Connection, `Where-Object`
changes.title: Explicit -<SwitchParameter>:$false corrected across thirteen cmdlets
changes.detail: Thirteen separate upstream PRs fixing one design mistake. This is the strongest argument for a single version-aware binder: fixing it per command would mean thirteen forks.

changes.subject: Unix formatting
changes.title: LastWriteTime column width is computed dynamically on Unix

changes.subject: formatting
changes.title: VT Reset sequences appearing mid-string are handled correctly
changes.detail: Only meaningful with a real ANSI parser. A formatter that treats escape sequences as ordinary characters cannot reproduce either the bug or the fix.

changes.subject: progress rendering
changes.title: Progress bar renders correctly with double-width Unicode characters
changes.detail: The archived v1 terminal already computes East Asian width correctly via its `dw()` helper; that behaviour must survive the rewrite rather than being reintroduced later.
